metadata.title: O/L ICT Complete (Grade 10 & 11) Domain-Specific Pronunciation Lexicon
metadata.description: Exhaustive technical vocabulary mapped from Sri Lankan O/L ICT national curriculum textbooks. Optimized for code-switched synthesis pipelines to prevent phonetic collapses on domain jargon, conjuncts, and loanwords.
metadata.ipa_format: plain (character-level phonemes concatenated with no separator within a word, words space-separated, punctuation preserved); English in eng_to_ipa's symbol set, affricates as tʃ / dʒ, Sinhala as spoken (unaspirated, ෂ = ʃ, schwa where everyday speech reduces /a/)

ict.risk: often mis-split by raw rule engines

data.risk: commonly read as US data; local standard is DAY-ta

cache.risk: must rhyme with cash, not cashay

ram.risk: must read as word, not spell out as letters

rom.risk: must read as word, not spell out as letters

ascii.expansion: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
ascii.risk: G2P engines often wrongly spell it out as letters

gui.risk: read as word gooey, must not spell out

router.risk: local standard prefers rooter over US rowter

lan.risk: must read as single word, not letters

ebcdic.expansion: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code

char.risk: Pascal data type, not 'char' as in charcoal

gif.risk: read as hard-g word, not spelled as letters

syndrome.risk: used in CVS, CTS, RSI expansions

apis.risk: plural acronym; default rule spells A-P-I-S

macos.risk: default rule cannot read mixed-case macOS

dusseldorf.risk: written Düsseldorf; the normaliser folds ü to u

blu.risk: Blu-ray, split at the hyphen by the normaliser
